image_description: A large, white radio telescope situated in an arid, grassy landscape with hills in the background. The telescope features a massive parabolic dish antenna mounted on a complex truss support structure. The dish is tilted upwards. The structure includes a visible receiver assembly suspended above the dish center by struts. The base appears to be a heavy steel framework on a concrete pad.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish is clearly the dominant feature, significantly larger than any other element in the frame, consistent with the 'colossal scale' description.
The side profile of the dish shows a smooth, continuous concave curve characteristic of a parabola. No irregularities or flattening are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive installation spanning an area visible from great distances.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Alt-azimuth or equatorial mount for celestial tracking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish is mounted on a complex yoke-like truss structure that allows rotation on two axes (elevation and azimuth), typical of alt-azimuth mounts used in modern radio telescopes.
The presence of the azimuth ring/base and the elevation trusses implies rotatability, which is structurally evident.
The base of the telescope rests on a substantial, dark-colored platform that appears to be concrete or heavy steel, anchoring the structure to the ground.
